extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI)
extraction.description: SCI is a multimodal benchmark comprising 20,000 self-contradictory instructions designed to evaluate the capability of large multimodal models to recognize and detect conflicting commands. It is evenly distributed between language-language and vision-language paradigms, spanning 8 tasks including RuleConflict, AttributeConflict, ExclusionConflict, ForbbidenConflict, OCRConflict, FigureConflict, GeometricConflict, and SemanticConflict. The dataset is constructed using an automatic dataset creation framework called AutoCreate.
extraction.creator: Jin Gao; Lei Gan; Yuankai Li; Yixin Ye; Dequan Wang
extraction.citeAs: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, and Dequan Wang. Dissecting Dissonance: Benchmarking Large Multimodal Models Against Self-Contradictory Instructions. arXiv:2408.01091v2 [cs.AI], 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The SCI benchmark was constructed using the AutoCreate automatic dataset creation framework, which combines large language models (LLMs) and programmatic generation. Starting from a small batch of manually input seeds, AutoCreate iteratively generates data through Language and Visual Loops, each consisting of a Generator, Decorator, and Cleaner. Language-language conflicts are generated via LLM prompting pipelines for each of the four task types. Vision-language conflicts are generated by creating images programmatically (varying font, size, color) and by retrieving images from the ImageNet dataset for SemanticConflict. Human experts double-check quality and manually select subsets (SCI-Core at 1%, SCI-Base at 10%).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection; Manual Human Curator; Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Manually crafted seed prompts; LLM-generated texts and instruction pairs; programmatically generated images (OCR, figure, geometric shapes); ImageNet dataset (imagenet-1k validation set) for SemanticConflict images.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human experts manually checked the quality of the AutoCreate-generated dataset and manually selected subsets (SCI-Core at 1% and SCI-Base at 10% of SCI-All). Human experts also evaluated LMM replies on SCI-Core to determine whether each reply successfully identified the conflict, providing ground-truth evaluation labels. An LLM agent (GPT-4) was also used as an evaluation agent and validated against human expert judgments.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Spearman correlation coefficient and concordance rate were calculated between human expert evaluations and LLM agent (GPT-4) evaluations on vision-language conflicts to measure consistency. GPT-4 showed high alignment with human evaluators (e.g., Spearman's rho of 0.881 and concordance of 94% for GPT-4V replies).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Large Language Models (LLMs) used in AutoCreate framework for generating and decorating dataset items (Generator, Decorator, Cleaner stages); GPT-4 used as evaluation agent; ImageNet dataset used for SemanticConflict image retrieval
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Only language-language and vision-language paradigms are included, excluding other modalities; SemanticConflict task relies on ImageNet dataset which may carry its own biases; LLM-generated data may reflect biases present in the underlying large language models used for AutoCreate
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Only language-language and vision-language paradigms are included; more modalities will be added in future work; no fine-grained control is introduced to determine the conflict degree; no detailed study on the attention mechanism of large multimodal models when confronted with conflict instructions
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Provides researchers and practitioners with a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs' ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction and communication technologies; the AutoCreate framework facilitates the creation of diverse instruction datasets, promoting inclusivity in AI research; improving dissonance detection boosts LMM performance and fosters trust and reliability in AI systems, essential for societal integration; self-contradictory instructions are particularly challenging for language beginners and vulnerable populations
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset does not contain personal or sensitive information; it consists of synthetically generated conflicting instructions and programmatically generated images (geometric shapes, charts, OCR text), with the only external data source being ImageNet images used for SemanticConflict
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the capability of large multimodal models to detect and recognize self-contradictory or conflicting instructions; benchmarking LMMs on language-language and vision-language instruction conflict tasks; training and evaluation of prompting approaches for dissonance detection in LMMs
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For FigureConflict, the numerical data is manipulated by changing the maximum value to the minimum value. For GeometricConflict, object descriptions are modified by exchanging the description of two attributes to refer to a non-existent object. For SemanticConflict, the correct class label in questions is substituted with a similar but different object. For OCRConflict, images vary in font, size, and color to augment diversity. For FigureConflict, charts are plotted with random choices for font, size, color, and other style options.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A Cleaner component removes data that does not meet quality standards. Both human experts and LLMs are involved in double-checking the quality of the generated dataset. For ForbbidenConflict, an LLM agent judges whether the answers to generated questions are unique, filtering out questions with ambiguous answers. Subsets SCI-Core (1%) and SCI-Base (10%) are selected manually from SCI-All, with extra effort to guarantee diversity for ExclusionConflict, ForbbidenConflict, and OCRConflict in SCI-Core.
